advisory_notice: All SQA findings, rankings and assessments are recommendations. Master decides whether, when and how to act through docs/plan.json.
priority_assessment: I would finish liveedit-size/do as planned. The scorecard has a 32 by 16 timing and still needs the 832 by 480 edit with a matching source clip. For faster commits, SQA-516 is still my first recommendation. The four landings after lanes-record spent 52 minutes combined in invariants and general tests. Only part of that work overlaps.

Before accepting a whole-run MOSS verdict, I would make it agree with the runner about missing checkpoints (SQA-517) and make a deleted fixture invalidate its reader's pass (SQA-415). Before another full measurement, I would settle publication-only retry (SQA-502) and which run owns a publication (SQA-474).

Before trusting another MOSS training proof, I would finish SQA-507 in the route that reads the pictures. The new identity reader can hash a different file from the encoder even when the corpus stays still.

findings.input: Land a production change with a fast step verifier and unchanged inputs between the two host test stages. An encoder-only production edit at 692c145aa exercised the scorecard-history fixture. On a refused landing, journey-attach/do, the step verifier itself failed in 9.7 s.
findings.expected: Keep cheap prerequisite checks early. Run the step verifier before unrelated long integration fixtures. Keep their distinct behavioral coverage in the ordinary suite and run each check once per unchanged candidate and inputs. Preserve the tagged whole-tree checks, undo evidence and coverage of inputs the gate edits.
findings.actual: invariants runs four full ordinary package suites before the step verifier. At 692c145aa the scorecard-history fixture took 66 s inside a 9 min 28 s stage before a 9 s verifier. On the refused journey-attach/do attempt, invariants took 215 s before the 9.7 s failure. After a passing verifier, test requests ./... again. At 6862d5287 the dispatch refusal test ran for 47 s then 41 s, and the trunk protection test for 29 s then 35 s. End-to-end savings are unmeasured.

findings.input: At the requested commit let the other lanes have current passes. In the models lane keep a current pass for TestMOSSSamplingCheckpoint and no result for the required TestMOSSGenerationCheckpoint after an interrupted run. All other retained models results are current. Ask validate -lanes-passed-at about that commit.
findings.expected: Report incomplete coverage and name the missing checkpoint. Judge the tests required at the requested commit with the lane's build tags and selection rules. Reading the verdict should not run the checkpoints. A result for a removed test should cease to count.
findings.actual: lanesPassedAt iterates only keys already in the result map. One current models pass and zero counted failures suffice, even when a required test has no key. The runner's testSteps lists the generation checkpoint and schedules it on the same inputs. Conversely, a retained failure for a deleted test in a still-selected package keeps the verdict red. Both cases follow from source at 4661a328c. The existing check covers empty results and a recorded stale result, but never one missing required result beside a current pass.

findings.input: After a passing needle-reference run, delete only fixtures/needle_upstream_calls.json and select lanes with -reached. The reader still names the old path. The same case applies to the models lane when only fixtures/moss/checkpoint.json is deleted.
findings.expected: A removed fixture invalidates its reader's prior pass. Where the reader cannot be resolved, the selector must cover the affected lane.
findings.actual: TrackedDocuments lists files still present. documentReaders omits the deleted fixture and discover returns no readers. In the landed per-test selector, stillCurrent treats that empty reach as proof that the prior pass is current, so -reached skips the check that would fail on the missing file. The retained fixture check covers edits while both files exist. The deletion case follows from source.

findings.input: In a full measurement let preflight, lanes and cells pass, then let publication alone fail before a scorecard is written. Retry the same run with matching commit, store, obligations and prerequisite inputs.
findings.expected: Retry publication with its completed cells and verified prerequisites. Recheck prerequisites when their inputs change or their successful completion cannot be established.
findings.actual: The launcher now admits a requested full scorecard through the cycle. On a publication-only retry measurePhases reads Cells and Published but invokes preflight and lanes before consulting either. The retained November 25 run spent 9 h 14 min 23 s in lanes. Repetition follows from source and the resume fixture. A retry duration has not been measured.

findings.input: While cycle C is checking its lanes, let another publisher write a scorecard for the same commit into the same store on a later clock second. Let C fail a required lane before it publishes.
findings.expected: C returns the lane error and keeps its retry state. Only a publication produced or explicitly credited by C supplies its proposals and permits Fill to clear that state. The existing publisher reports the path it wrote.
findings.actual: Measure treats an increase in the directory's record count as proof of publication and returns the newest record if its commit matches. Improve proposes from that record and calls Fill even with the lane error. Fill removes C's phase and cell credit. This follows from source. The retained case with an unchanged directory already rejects the older record.

findings.input: In two MOSS corpora, put one leading space before red.png in the manifest's path field. Give both directories the same red.png and different valid pictures named ' red.png'. Use the same caption, weights and size. Separately, replace held-out picture B with same-size training picture A after split admission and before preparation.
findings.expected: Derive the recipe and proof identities from the ordered inputs the route admits and consumes. Preserve its path syntax and relocation behavior. Consume the admitted media or verify their identity on reread so a changed training clip or substituted held-out picture is caught.
findings.actual: MediaManifestBytes trims the line before extracting the path and hashes red.png. mossManifest preserves the leading space and mossPrepare encodes ' red.png'. The two static corpora therefore train on different pixels under the same dataset identity. MOSS also reopens held-out paths after checking the split, and the codec reopens clips after hashing, without comparing either reread to the admitted input. These are source counterexamples at 07a7a7185.

findings.input: Start the landing fixture with unformatted internal/p/p.go. After gofmt writes it and recordWrites records that path, append a separate, valid function for the next step to the same file before fix calls shipSet. The first step’s assertion on the original function still passes.
findings.expected: Publish only the first candidate and the gate’s edits to those bytes. Leave the later function in the checkout for its own step. Use the existing candidate or keep the exact output of the transformation. The snapshot fixture can distinguish both copies with this same-file edit.
findings.actual: b9bac4955 protects other paths, including later.go and notes.txt in the existing fixture. recordWrites keeps a boolean for p.go after comparing its hashes. A later capture starts at the first tree but stages the current checkout bytes of every gateWrote path, including the later function in p.go. The earlier cross-step landing was observed at b1d6e237a. This remaining case was established from source at 70394cb96.

findings.input: A named lead holds the worktree and has asked to pause. Before its stop is recorded, the prompt hook receives a progress question without a session_id. The harness’s nameless-hook path is covered in sessions_test.go.
findings.expected: Preserve the holder’s pending stop request. Only a prompt attributable to the holding session should change its authorization. A nameless hook may still take its existing shared turn snapshot.
findings.actual: be631dfc3 fixes the named reviewer and visitor cases and the direct negation “don’t stop.” With no session_id, holdWorktree returns an empty string before reading the holder. beginTurn treats that value as permission to call NoteStopRequest, which removes the lead’s request on the progress prompt. RequireStopRequest then refuses the authorized pause. This residual case follows from source. No missed pause was observed.

findings.input: A serving or training observation published by servingattempt.Record or trainingworkflow.Observer.finish when (a) the recipe-state read fails and the incoming Verification is empty, or (b) the same recipe is activated again, verified, after the recorded attempt executed it not verified.
findings.expected: Publication carries the state the executed recipe and task had at execution. A failed state read is told apart from a historical absent state and earns no verified credit, and a later activation does not replace execution-time state. Legacy bytes, the own-verifying-run exception and partial or cancelled results keep their contract.
findings.actual: servingattempt.Record and Observer.finish read recipe state when publishing and drop lookup errors. A failed read can leave Verification empty, which unverifiedAside accepts as legacy. A later activation of the same recipe can supply verified state for an attempt that ran unverified. Both cases follow from source.

findings.input: Select stored PNG A, then B, for a MOSS image-to-image slot. Let B's fetch finish first, then submit after both complete. In depth control, ask for A's preview, switch to B and back to A before the response, display it, then choose B once more.
findings.expected: Submit B in the first case and clear A's map on the final switch to B in the second. Set a stored-picture slot from the clicked artifact ID and MIME type. Download bytes for attachments that consume them. Associate a displayed preview with its current picture and settings.
findings.actual: mediaCard fetches a blob before calling reuse. The older response can overwrite B's artifact ID with A's. In depthPreview the first switch to B clears showing. A's response can then display after the return to A without restoring showing, so the final switch to B leaves A's map visible. Both event orders follow from source. The existing checks cover a single card and a single switch away.

findings.input: For calibration, guess two independent three-choice questions on each of 32 independent media. Compare constant judge scores, then grouped probabilities (.9,.1) and (.45,.45). For admission, compare GIF arms decoded at 16 frames and one. In the embedded SenseNova APG verdict keep its evaluation IDs, set 0 wins, 524 losses, 0 ties, 80 media, Tail=.0001 and Admitted=true, and match the displayed counts and gain wording. For recovery, resume with a build that changes an earlier reused draw but reproduces the last one, or a verdict line truncated after the arm name and the opening JSON brace.
findings.expected: Validate calibration against the chance distribution of the questions on each medium. Rank using the production aggregation and report an undefined interval for tied scores. Bind preset admission to comparable questions, decoding, producer, judge and request. Derive counts and tails from the bound evaluations. Credit a resumed result only when its inputs and evidence still match.
findings.actual: The sign test assumes a fair sign, but the guessing case is positive with probability 5/9. It clears the nominal 5% threshold 9.14% of the time. Arithmetic means reverse softShare's geometric ranking on the given pair. Constant scores leave resampledTau indexing an empty slice. judgedRender omits decode and question identity, readRender reads the manifest without verifying its draws, and admission resolves the current activation. The offering uses stored flags and tail by model name and preset. A consistently worded 0-win APG gain passes verdictSaid and Gained. Recovery skips arms and verdicts by name, skips an existing suite, and checks only the last reused draw before drawing more at a new build. These are source and arithmetic counterexamples.

findings.input: Record two different PNGs returned by node 449 with the same basename original.png in subfolders MOSS/a and MOSS-a of the same recording.
findings.expected: Keep each output under a distinct name and leave both recorded hashes verifiable. The recorder already computes the content hash and its existing two-output case can check both names and bytes.
findings.actual: keep replaces each slash in the subfolder with a hyphen. Both responses are written as 449-MOSS-a-original.png. The second write replaces the first, leaving two hashes for one path and causing verification of the first entry to fail. Source counterexample.

findings.input: A retained ClipMotion observation of unchanged MP4 bytes, then a motion encoder checkpoint or FFmpeg/preprocessing configuration changes under the same encoder basename. The suite is compiled again with that old observation and the same matching clip-content digest.
findings.expected: Bind the observation to the encoder checkpoint and decoding and sampling settings used to produce it. Reuse a motion reading only when that identity and the clip content both match.
findings.actual: writeMotion passes the encoder basename. ClipMotion.validate checks that it is nonempty, and bindObservations compares the clip content. A changed checkpoint under the same name, or changed decoding settings on identical bytes, therefore leaves the old metric admissible. Source counterexample.
